rubric.task_read: This is a trivially short, single-token edit: locate one instance of 'recieve' in README.md and change it to 'receive', touching nothing else. The horizon is minutes, the environment is one known file, and the contract is fully specified. A skilled practitioner invests almost no meta-work — just find, fix, and a quick glance to confirm exactly one word changed. Over-investment (plans, milestone tracking, verification harnesses) would be pure ceremony here.

dimensions.name: Locating the typo
dimensions.description: Confirming where 'recieve' appears in README.md before editing, rather than guessing at a replacement.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The edit tool needs an exact match and the spec says the word appears 'once'; a single grep/read to find the line prevents editing the wrong text or missing the occurrence.

anchors.0: Edits or attempts to edit without ever locating the word; blind find-and-replace on a guessed string.
anchors.3: Opens README.md and eyeballs it without pinpointing the occurrence.
anchors.5: Greps or reads README.md and identifies the exact line/context containing 'recieve' before editing.
anchors.8: Locates the occurrence AND confirms it is the only one (e.g. grep count), ensuring the 'once' assumption holds.
anchors.10: Precisely locates and count-verifies the single occurrence, noting surrounding context to guarantee a unique, unambiguous replacement — with zero wasted exploration.

dimensions.name: Task breakdown
dimensions.description: Whether the trivial single-step edit is treated as the atomic action it is.
dimensions.why_it_matters: This task is a single atomic edit; decomposition beyond 'find then replace' is unwarranted overhead.

anchors.0: N/A — a single edit cannot really lack structure; scored low regardless.
anchors.5: Recognizes it as one atomic action and proceeds directly, no artificial subdivision.
anchors.8: Rare here: any structuring beyond find/fix would be over-investment.
anchors.10: Not meaningfully reachable; elaborate milestone plans would be ceremony and should be penalized as over-investment.

dimensions.name: Confirming the one-word change
dimensions.description: Checking that exactly 'recieve'→'receive' happened and nothing else was altered.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The spec is strict ('Do not modify anything else'); a quick post-edit check (diff or re-grep) confirms correctness and scope compliance cheaply.

anchors.0: No check at all; assumes the edit worked and moved on.
anchors.3: Casual assumption of success with maybe a glance.
anchors.5: Verifies the word was changed (re-read the line or grep for 'receive'/absence of 'recieve').
anchors.8: Confirms the change AND that scope was respected — e.g. git diff showing exactly one word on one line altered.
anchors.10: Tight, targeted verification: diff proving a single-character-class change on one line, confirms no other occurrences remain, no collateral edits — proportionate and complete.

dimensions.name: Tracking a one-step task
dimensions.description: Maintaining awareness of done-vs-remaining across a task that is essentially one action.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With a single step there is almost nothing to monitor; awareness is trivially satisfied by completing the edit.

anchors.0: Loses track — re-edits, forgets whether the change was made, or leaves it ambiguous.
anchors.3: Completes the edit with implicit awareness it is done.
anchors.5: Clearly knows the task is complete after the single edit.
anchors.8: Not meaningfully distinguishable from adequate on a one-step task.
anchors.10: Not reachable without over-engineering; elaborate progress tracking here is ceremony.

dimensions.name: Handling surprises
dimensions.description: Reacting if reality diverges — e.g. the word doesn't appear, appears zero or multiple times, or the edit fails to match.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The only plausible course-correction is if the 'once' assumption is wrong or the exact-match edit fails; a skilled agent adjusts rather than forcing a bad edit.

anchors.0: On a failed match or unexpected count, retries blindly or edits the wrong text.
anchors.3: If the edit fails, makes a reasonable second attempt.
anchors.5: If the occurrence isn't where expected or count differs, re-checks and adjusts the approach accordingly.
anchors.8: Anticipates the divergence (e.g. checks count first) and handles a zero/multiple-occurrence case correctly without thrashing.
anchors.10: Fully robust: detects any mismatch between spec ('once') and reality, resolves it correctly and minimally, and never forces an incorrect edit — though the task rarely provides occasion to display this.
